Our read of the dirty table cannot keep order for the partition table.

issue_context.title: UnionScan with partition table + keepOrder can't get correct result
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```
create table t(a int, b int, primary key(b)) PARTITION BY HASH(b) partitions 4;
analyze table t;
begin;
insert into t(a, b) values (6,6),(3,3),(9,9),(4,4),(5,5),(7,7),(8,8);
select * from t where b > 1 order by b limit 5;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

```
mysql> select * from t where b > 1 order by b limit 5;
+------+---+
| a    | b |
+------+---+
|    3 | 3 |
|    4 | 4 |
|    5 | 5 |
|    6 | 6 |
|    7 | 7 |
+------+---+
5 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```
mysql> select * from t where b > 1 order by b limit 5;
+------+---+
| a    | b |
+------+---+
|    4 | 4 |
|    8 | 8 |
|    5 | 5 |
|    9 | 9 |
|    6 | 6 |
+------+---+
5 rows in set (0.00 sec)
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
comments:
1. We can disable pushdown `topN` when `UnionScan` exists firstly.
2. And let `UnionScan` support partition table in next step.
`set tidb_partition_prune_mode = 'static'` seems unaffected (since it sees each partition as a separate table), but the `dynamic` tidb_partition_prune_mode is affected by this bug.

review_comments: Maybe add `failpoint.Enable("github.com/pingcap/tidb/planner/core/forceDynamicPrune", 'return(true)')` here, I found it not always use dynamic pruning for this situation.
We can add one line to set the session variable.
